correctness.rationale: The Palm/Mecke two-point integral uses the union of the two radius-r sector exclusion regions; radial integration yields 1/(2U). Opposite-direction overlap has two arcs of width alpha-pi, and horizontal reflection gives the single-angular-interval formula. At pi, the right-half-disc overlap is half the classical radius-one unit-separation lens, yielding U=2pi/3+sqrt(3)/4 and the strict positive linear coefficient. For empirical convergence, truncated nearest neighbor reciprocity is measurable inside radius 2T, its variance per area is bounded by finite-range two-point independence, the missing-tail probability is exactly exp(-alpha T^2/2) away from boundary, and boundary area is negligible. 40 numerical diagnostics replayed from verify.py, which are not used as infinite proofs.

value.rationale: The motivating 2026 paper specifically identifies reflex-sector nearest-neighbor graphs as an unexplored regime. Mutual two-cycles are a natural local and empirical network statistic that are absent for all nonreflex sectors. A strictly positive linear onset with an exact geometric coefficient, a full sector-parameter quadrature and an empirical high-intensity law constitute a meaningful structural phase transition, rather than a trivial sample-size substitution or recomputation of the unrestricted planar constant.
